name: Titus Mountain
generated_description:
Titus Mountain is a 1,522-foot summit in Connecticut. The Titus Mountain Trail covers 2.3 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 213 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Most of the climbing comes early — the first half of the route does the bulk of the work before the grade eases. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0, gaining roughly 800 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 1,204 feet, the route tops out near 1,417 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 41.91617, -73.30397 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 35 miles west of Hartford, Connecticut. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Howe Mountain, Sedgwick Mountain and Stone Man Mountain — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 41.91617, -73.30397 in Connecticut. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Titus Mountain?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Titus Mountain?
faqs.answer: Titus Mountain stands at 1,522 feet (464 meters) in Connecticut.
